summary: Madeleine Biardeau studied at École normale supérieure de jeunes filles from circa 1943 to 1946. Active in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, she served as enseignante at École Pratique des Hautes Études from 1961 to 1989.
Madeleine Zelin is a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology. She studied at Cornell University (~1966–1970) and UC Berkeley (~1970–1979), and took up a post at Columbia University around 1979.
Madhav Krishna Sharma was an Indology scholar who studied under C. Kunhan Raja. In 1952, he held a post as Inspector in the Department of Sanskrit Education, Rajasthan.
Madhu Khanna is a scholar in the fields of Indology and religious studies. She has held posts at Jamia Millia Islamia and the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts.

Madhukar Anant Mehendale worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as Joint Secretary of the Linguistic Society of India (1954–1955) and as Professor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute around 1958.
Madhusudan Dhaky studied at Fergusson College and worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Associate Director at the American Institute of Indian Studies from circa 1976 to 1996.

Mae Chee Huynh Kim Lan is a Buddhist studies scholar. She completed a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (~2008–2010), advised by Phra Suthithammanuwat and Veerachart Nimanong.

Maheshachandra Nyayaratna Bhattacharyya studied Indology and philosophy under Edward Byles Cowell (~1858–1864). He succeeded Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar and served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University from circa 1876 to 1895.

Mahinda Deegalle studied at Harvard Divinity School (~1989–1991) and the University of Chicago (~1991–1997) under Diana L. Eck, Frank E. Reynolds, and Wendy Doniger. He held posts at Harvard, Bath Spa University, and Colgate University.
Maho Iuchi works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Otani University by 2008 and has served as a guest researcher (客員研究員) at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies.
Mai Mishiro is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She has held posts at Waseda University and the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science.

Makio Takemura studied at the University of Tokyo (~1970–1975) and worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. His academic career included posts at the University of Tokyo, Mie University, the University of Tsukuba, Rissho University, and Toyo University.
Makio Ueno earned a PhD from Otani University by 2009 and specializes in Buddhist studies. Ueno has held an assistant professor (助教) post at Otani University.
Makoto Funaoka studied at Meiji University (~1965–1974) and worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He was a professor (教授) at Hokkai-Gakuen University from circa 1989 to 2017.

Makoto Nagai studied at the University of Tokyo (~1904–1907) and worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held academic posts at the University of Tokyo (~1927–1942) and Toyo University (~1946–1957).

Makoto Nagamura studied at Azabu Junior and Senior High School (~1961–1967) and worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as a professor (教授) at Japan Women's University from circa 1993 to 2017.
Makoto Yoshimura studied doctoral coursework at Waseda University (~1996–2001) in Buddhist studies and sinology. In 2004, Yoshimura held a post as associate professor (助教授) at Komazawa University.

Malcolm David Eckel studied at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi (~1975–1980), working in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held posts as Professor at Harvard (~1980–1990) and Associate Professor of Religion at Boston University (~1990–2001).
Mamoru Tonami studied at Kyoto University from circa 1956 to 1965, working in sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He later held a post at Otani University from circa 2000 to 2011.
Manabendu Banerjee is an Indologist who served as Secretary of the Asiatic Society until 2000. He also held a post at Jadavpur University as Co-ordinator of DSA Sanskrit.
